adiabatic-conditions-a0-a3: Section 1.1, p.2: the paper states (A0)-(A3) as the conditions of its own result. Value matches the text.
adiabatic-path-need-not-be-linear: Section 1.1, p.2: the authors state their own setup does not require a linear interpolation, and give the reason in parentheses.
technique-limit-non-ff-stoquastic: Section 1.1, p.3: the authors state their technique does not permit efficient simulation for stoquastic Hamiltonians that are not frustration-free. A limit on their own method.
open-general-stoquastic-adiabatic: Section 1.1, p.3: the authors state this as their own open question, that is, what their results do not settle.
scope-k-local-polynomial-bounds: Definition 1.1 text, p.2: 'We shall consider families of k-local Hamiltonians in which k = O(1), M <= poly(n), and ||Ha|| <= poly(n)'. The paper's own scope.
def-1-6-constraint-system-unsat: Definition 1.6 and the unsat-value definition, p.3: match the value.
def-1-7-1-8-stoquastic-k-sat: Definitions 1.7 and 1.8, p.3-4: match the value, including epsilon = n^-O(1) and the yes/no conditions.
stoquastic-k-sat-is-promise-problem: Section 1.1, p.4: the paper defines stoquastic k-SAT as the promise problem (Lyes, Lno) with explicit sets.
stoquastic-k-sat-np-hard-k-ge-3: Section 1.1, p.4: the paper gives the reduction itself: diagonal constraints with entries 0,1 make classical k-SAT a special case, so NP-hardness for k>=3 follows. The NP-hardness of classical k-SAT is textbook background. The reduction is two sentences and does not spell out the epsilon gap, so this is the thinnest HIGH in the group.
thm-1-9-stoquastic-k-sat-in-ma: Theorem 1.9 first sentence, p.4, with its condition (constant k). Section 6.1 (completeness, p.15-16) and 6.2 (soundness, p.16-17) prove it from Lemma 4.5 and the verifier of p.14-15, with no cited theorem as a step. The finite-precision remark is separate (see soundness-with-finite-precision-sampling).
one-step-of-walk-efficiently-simulable: Section 2.1, p.5-6: the paper argues from O(1)-qubit terms that at most poly(n) strings y have P>0, and uses Eq. (2.4) (proved as Lemma 4.5) to compute the probabilities. The argument is complete in the paper, though short.
satisfying-assignment-supported-on-good-: Section 2.3, p.7 states it; Lemma 4.4(1), p.10, proves that x in S(psi) gives <x|Pi|x> > 0 when Pi|psi>=|psi>, which is exactly S(psi) subset of Sgood.
coherent-gibbs-state-unique-ground-state: Section 3.1, p.8-9: credited to [18,19], but the paper gives its own derivation: X_j|pi> = Gamma_j|pi>, Gamma_j diagonal real and local (needs the constant-terms-per-qubit condition, quoted), H_beta|pi>=0, Perron-Frobenius for uniqueness, and each local term PSD. The proof is in the paper.
prop-4-1-spectral-projector-nonnegative: Proposition 4.1, p.9: stated with its condition, proved in the next lines as the limit of e^{-beta H}/Z.
lemma-4-2-nonnegative-projector-block-st: Lemma 4.2, p.9, proved on p.10 with connected components and Perron-Frobenius (a textbook tool).
cor-4-3-nonnegative-ground-state-basis: Corollary 4.3, p.10: follows at once from Proposition 4.1 and Lemma 4.2, both proved in the paper. Both are combined in the text.
lemma-5-1-ground-state-overlap: Lemma 5.1, p.11, proved on p.12 from Eq. (5.1) and the gap. The paper says a more general version is in [17] but proves this one itself.
warm-start-definition: Section 5, p.13, Eq. (5.5): 'A string x(j) satisfying Eq. (5.5) will be referred to as a warm start'. A definition.
mixing-from-warm-start-error-bound: Section 5, p.13: derived from the walk definition, Cauchy-Schwarz, and the largest eigenvalue of G~ at most 1 - beta*Delta (from Proposition 5.2). The bound 2^{n+1}(1-beta*Delta)^L follows with the warm-start bound 2^{-n-2}. It is an inequality, not a simplified step. It rests on Proposition 5.2, which the paper only asserts, but the gap there is the paper's own definition-level step.
lemma-5-4-t-balanced-probability: Lemma 5.4, p.13, with conditions F>=1-delta and t>=4 quoted; proved in full on p.13-14 (bound sqrt(pi rho) <= t^{-1/2}(pi+rho) off the balanced set). The bound 1 - 2*delta/(1-2 t^{-1/2}) follows from the last line; the text layer garbles Eq. (5.7) but the proof is complete.
prop-5-5-probability-lower-bound-on-samp: Proposition 5.5, p.14: stated for any distribution and proved in one line (at most 2^n strings, each below 2^-2n, so mass at most 2^-n).
proof-sketch-neglects-exponentially-smal: Section 5, p.13 and p.14: the authors state they neglect exponentially small errors and events 'for simplicity'. A limit the paper states on its own proof.
verifier-protocol-setup: Section 6, p.14-15: the paper states the prover's strategy, the choice of beta and L (Eq. 6.1) and Steps 1-9 of its own protocol.
completeness-yes-instance-prob-one: Section 6.1, p.15-16: proved from Lemma 4.5 (r_j = ratio of amplitudes, product telescopes, w has largest amplitude so the product is at most 1). The precision remark is stated with its conditions.
soundness-no-instance-prob-at-most-one-t: Section 6.2, p.16-17: proved. The sum is bounded by 2^{n/2}<x0|G^L|+>, the largest eigenvalue of G is at most 1 - epsilon*beta/M by the no-instance promise, and Eq. (6.1) gives at most 1/3. No cited theorem is used as a step.
discussion-derandomization-open: Section 7, p.18: the authors state the derandomization question as open.
open-ratio-of-amplitudes-no-efficient-al: Section 7, p.18: the authors state that for general stoquastic Hamiltonians their walk needs the ratio of amplitudes, for which no efficient algorithm is known. A limit on their own approach.
def-7-1-promise-ma: Definition 7.1, Appendix A, p.19: matches the value.
def-ma-complete-promise-problem: Appendix A, p.19: the paper defines MA-completeness for promise problems with the map f. Matches the value.
prop-1-5-proof-ground-state-overlap: Appendix B, p.20-21: with the explicit ground state (L+1)^{-1/2} sum |psi_j>|j>_u, the last (1-delta)L gates identity means psi_j = psi_L for at least a (1-delta) fraction of j, so the overlap with |psi_L>|A> is at least 1-delta. This is a direct computation. It covers only the overlap step, not the gap bound.
ma-hardness-constraints-stoquastic-6-loc: Appendix B, p.21: from the paper's own constraints (7.2), (7.3): ancillas |0>, |+> and Toffoli gates give off-diagonals 0 or -1/2, the clock and measurement terms are diagonal, n = N+L+1. It is a conditional statement about the paper's own construction, given the transformed verifier V'. The 6-locality count is only stated.

theory_low.thm-1-4-classical-simulation-of-sff-adia: Theorem 1.4, p.2, is stated with (A0)-(A3). Section 5, p.11-14, proves it only after the paper says it neglects exponentially small errors and ignores exponentially small events 'for simplicity' (p.13, p.14), and the failure bound uses approximate signs (about, ~). A bound argued informally, so not the proved-result basis.
theory_low.prop-1-5-ff-adiabatic-universal: Proposition 1.5, p.3, is called 'a simple extension of [2]' and Appendix B, p.19-20, only 'outlines the proof'. The proof uses the gap bound Omega(1/L^2) from Lemma 3.11 of [2] and the improved estimates of [21], both cited. A proof that rests on specific other papers' results is not proved-result.
theory_low.ff-alone-not-classically-simulable: Section 1.1, p.2-3: the authors' interpretation ('implies ... as hard as simulating a universal quantum computer') of Proposition 1.5, which is itself LOW (outline resting on [2] and [21]).
theory_low.thm-1-9-stoquastic-6-sat-ma-hard: Theorem 1.9 second part, p.4. The proof (Section 2.4, p.8; Appendix B, p.21) is a repeat of Lemma 2 of [7], and uses 'the derivation of [3]' for the eigenvalue bound. It rests on cited results of other papers, so not proved-result.
theory_low.transition-probabilities-normalized-good: Section 2.3, p.7: normalization of Eq. (2.7) is asserted as following from the rank-one block property, 'see Section 4 for details', with no derivation. The good-to-bad remark is only an observation.
theory_low.coherent-probabilistic-computation-sff: Section 3.2, p.9 and Appendix B, p.21: the claim is stated, then 'completely analogous to the proof of Proposition 1.5', which is an outline resting on [2] and [21]. No proof given here.
theory_low.lemma-4-4-nonneg-projector-support: Lemma 4.4, p.10-11: the paper proves it in full (part 1 by contradiction, part 2 via Lemma 4.2). But the quotes drop the hypothesis Pi|psi>=|psi> for a non-negative state and Eq. (4.1). The rule grades a result whose conditions the quotes drop as LOW. Regrade to HIGH (proved result) if the quotes are extended to carry the hypothesis and Eq. (4.1).
theory_low.lemma-4-5-amplitude-ratio-from-ha: Lemma 4.5, p.11: the proof is in the paper and uses Lemma 4.4 and Proposition 4.1. But the quotes drop the hypotheses (SFF Hamiltonian, H|psi>=0 for a non-negative state) and the ratio identity. Conditions dropped, so LOW. Would be HIGH (proved result) with fuller quotes.
theory_low.prop-5-2-gap-of-g-and-walk: Proposition 5.2, p.12: the properties of G(j) (non-negative, spectrum in [0,1], unique eigenvalue 1, gap >= beta*Delta) are said to 'follow directly from the definition'. No derivation is given. Only the walk-gap step (similarity transformation) is argued.
theory_low.warm-start-propagation-and-failure-proba: Section 5, p.14: the conditional probability is derived while 'ignoring ... events that occur with exponentially small probability'. The failure bound uses approximations ((1-x)^T ~ 1-xT, 'delta ~ J^2 D^-2 T^-1'). Informal, not proved-result.
theory_low.soundness-with-finite-precision-sampling: Section 6.2, p.17: 'One can easily verify' the trajectory-difference bound L*delta, with no derivation. The amplification to 1/3 by 'standard majority voting' is asserted, not shown.
theory_low.simplified-sat-satisfiable-iff-good-comp: Section 6.3, p.17: the iff is stated with 'One can easily observe'. Only the 'if' direction (sum over a good component is a satisfying state) is sketched. No proof of the converse.
theory_low.simplified-sat-block-structure: Section 6.3, p.17: block structure (blocks of 0, 1, or (1/2)[[1,1],[1,1]], none above dimension two) is stated as following from Pi=Pi^2. No derivation is given, though it would follow from Lemma 4.2 plus the entry set.
theory_low.clock-hamiltonian-is-frustration-free: Appendix B, p.20: this is Kitaev's clock Hamiltonian construction from [3]. The paper asserts the terms are positive semi-definite and that the path subspace is the zero space, without checking. 'All these results follow directly from the clock Hamiltonian construction of [3]'. Cited construction, not proved here.
theory_low.smooth-interpolation-of-gates: Appendix B, p.20: the smooth interpolation follows from connectivity of SU(N), but satisfying (A2) uses the gap bound Omega(1/L^2) from Lemma 3.11 of [2] and [21]. The value claims the whole family satisfies (A1)-(A3), which rests on cited results.
theory_low.ma-hardness-reduction-gap: Appendix B, p.21: the transformation of a classical MA verifier to V' is Lemma 2 of [7], and the lower bound on the smallest eigenvalue is 'the derivation of [3]'. The reduction rests on these cited results, so not proved-result.
theory_low.constraints-as-i-minus-nonneg-projector: Appendix B, p.21: 'we remark that any constraint from the system C can be represented as I - Pi ...' with no derivation.
